articles.title:
Austria Moves to Ban Social Media for Children Under 14 Amid
Growing EU Safety Push
articles.excerpt:
Austria's conservative-led coalition government announced
plans on March 27, 2026, to prohibit social media access for children
under 14, citing addiction risks and harmful content. The legislation,
expected by summer 2026, follows a nationwide school experiment
involving 72,000 pupils and aligns with similar restrictions emerging
across France, Spain, and Denmark. The move comes as a U.S. jury
recently held Meta liable for endangering minors, intensifying
pressure on tech platforms across Western democracies.

articles.title:
Hungary's Election Campaign Roiled by Russian Interference
Claims and Energy Dispute
articles.excerpt:
With less than a month until Hungary's parliamentary election
on 12 April, allegations of Russian meddling and a bitter dispute over
oil pipeline repairs have intensified an already polarized campaign.
Opposition leader Péter Magyar has accused Prime Minister Viktor Orbán
of treason for allegedly enabling Russian interference, while a
standoff with Ukraine over the Druzhba pipeline threatens energy
security. The contest pits Orbán's nationalist, Russia-friendly stance
against Magyar's pro-European vision, with polls showing a tight race
that could reshape Hungary's relationship with Brussels.

articles.title:
Slovakia's Fico Weathers Protests Over Pro-Russian Tilt as
Election Year Looms
articles.excerpt:
Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico has consolidated power
despite sustained protests against his government's halt to Ukraine
military aid and opposition to EU sanctions on Russia. Thousands of
demonstrators, led by students, have demanded his resignation over
what they call a pro-Russian betrayal of Slovakia's Western alliances.
With parliamentary elections scheduled for 2026, Fico's
sovereignty-focused foreign policy is deepening political polarization
and testing the country's commitment to NATO and EU
solidarity.

articles.title:
Austria's New Coalition Struggles as Far-Right FPÖ Surges in
Polls
articles.excerpt:
Austria's three-party coalition government, formed in March
2025 after excluding the election-winning Freedom Party, faces
mounting instability as the far-right FPÖ polls at 35-37 percent. The
coalition's adoption of hardline immigration policies, including a
controversial anti-Muslim campaign, has failed to stem public
discontent. Analysts warn the fragile arrangement may not survive as
voters express anger over the exclusion of the party that won the most
votes in 2024.

articles.title:
Slovakia's Fico Navigates US-Russia Balancing Act as
Election Year Deepens EU Rift
articles.excerpt:
Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico is pursuing a foreign
policy that maintains Russian energy ties while courting the Trump
administration, creating friction with EU institutions and domestic
opposition ahead of 2026 elections. A major nuclear deal with
Washington has delivered economic gains, but unresolved US tariff
threats and persistent energy dependence on Moscow leave Slovakia
exposed to conflicting pressures. The approach has intensified
polarization between government supporters who praise pragmatic
sovereignty and critics who warn of democratic erosion and diplomatic
isolation.

articles.title:
Hungary's Opposition Faces Uphill Battle Against Electoral
System as Fidesz Deploys Anti-War Rallies
articles.excerpt:
With four weeks until Hungary's April 12 election, rival mass
rallies in Budapest have exposed deep polarization between Prime
Minister Viktor Orbán's Fidesz party and surging opposition leader
Péter Magyar. While independent polls show Magyar's Tisza party
leading by double digits, Hungary's electoral system requires the
opposition to win by oversized margins to overcome structural
advantages built into the voting framework. The contest has become a
referendum on Orbán's 16-year rule, frozen EU funds, and Hungary's
geopolitical orientation.
